text:
maya: quick thread to lock the long-term routing + isolation commitments for the Q3 roadmap. need to finalize scope by Fri so PMs can split epics.

owen: can we separate short-term ship (MVP) vs runway work (6-12mo)? i worry backlog will mix infra debt with product asks.

raj: high-level runway items i think are non-negotiable: 1) routing policy precedence matrix, 2) cross-region graceful failover semantics, 3) tenant soft/hard eviction contract, 4) residency & data-path controls for private deployments.

carla: customer asks summary from Sales: two enterprise deals require per-tenant residency + signed SLA for Dedicated; one health-care customer asked for clear eviction notification + audit trail.

maya: proposal: MVP (ship in Q2 end) = policy precedence + basic region affinity + soft-evict playbook + console telemetry. Runway (Q3-Q4) = model-aware cost routing, per-tenant override webhooks, residency enforcement, hard-evict automation for Dedicated.

sales_eng: emphasize: the residency bit can't be "later" for those two deals. Legal needs contract language now. can we commit to a private-deploy baseline by Q3?

own: technical constraints: hard-evict automation requires persistent KV-cache sharding and an eviction API that can chop in-flight KV ranges safely. that's a non-trivial infra project. estimate 6 weeks core work + 2 weeks validation.

raj: risk note: cross-region reroute spikes will amplify autoscaling costs. finance asked for a routing budget cap per-tenant by default (e.g., 10% spend delta). we need a circuit to prefer cheaper compatible model variants under constrained capacity.

carla: from product side: launch criteria checklist we should lock:
- documented policy precedence matrix (owner: raj)
- canary plan with 3 tenants and rollback playbook (owner: owen)
- tenant-facing eviction runbook and notification template (owner: carla)
- legal-ready residency language draft (owner: sales_eng)

maya: agree. also add acceptance tests: simulate 2-region outage, assert failover within 2m and no data leakage; simulate burst failover, assert throttle prevents >2x baseline throughput spike.

own: small config example for the precedence table (ops-friendly YAML):
```
policies:
  - name: "customer-overrides"
    precedence: 100
  - name: "dedicated-isolation"
    precedence: 90
  - name: "geo-affinity"
    precedence: 50
  - name: "cost-aware-fallback"
    precedence: 10
```

raj: nice. also wire telemetry tags: policy.name, action (route/evict/failover), cost-delta, evict-reason. critical for postmortems and for Optimize recommendations.

carla: customer-facing timeline:
- EOW: firmed acceptance checklist + policy doc draft
- 2 weeks: acceptance tests implemented in staging + earliest canary window
- Q3: residency enforcement beta for Private customers

sales_eng: legal wants the residency beta caveats up front. i'll draft and loop in contracts.

infra-bot: created ticket RW-4822 (routing-policy-precedence) assigned to raj, due 2026-05-07.

maya: owners recap and hard asks:
- raj: policy precedence doc + telemetry tags (due Thu)
- owen: canary plan + automated rollback playbook (due Thu)
- carla: tenant runbook + customer notifications (due Fri)
- sales_eng: residency contract draft (due Fri)

raj: added a placeholder risk: if we push model-aware routing into MVP, pushback from finance + complexity for rollback. recommend keeping it in runway.

maya: decision: keep MVP conservative (affinity + soft-evict + visibility). runway will include hard-evict automation and residency enforcement.

own: sample canary CLI for ops to run once tests pass:
```
redwoodctl routing canary --policy precedence-mvp --tenants tenant-alpha,tenant-beta,tenant-gamma --pct 3 --duration 72h
```

maya: closing: please update tickets and PRD sections before EOD. we'll take any objections in tomorrow's sync, otherwise this is the plan. :checkered_flag:
